title: Message boards, i
logline: The chorus has grown. Twelve stick figures. They have opinions about SLASH, which they've never seen.

panels.composition: The garage. WOOD at the monitor. At the back of the panel, twelve stick figures, a crowd now, some with signs: MORE DOG · WHERE IS THE NOVEL · THE SUNDAYS ARE THE ONLY GOOD PART.

image.prompt: a young man at a bulky computer in a garage with twelve small stick figures crowded at the back of the panel, several holding crude signs, muddy digital flats
image.notes: Signs: MORE DOG / WHERE IS THE NOVEL / THE SUNDAYS ARE THE ONLY GOOD PART. Letter after.

panels.composition: Wood, turning, a stack of the novel's pages in his hand.

characters.pose: holding up pages to the chorus

balloons.text: The novel is here. Five hundred pages. It's serious. It's about a timber town and—

image.prompt: a young man holding up a stack of drawn pages toward a crowd of stick figures, defensive

panels.composition: The monitor: he's posted one page. A noir page. Below it, the comments box. The strip draws the number: 0 comments.

image.prompt: close-up of a monitor showing a dark noir-styled comic page with a comment count of zero beneath it

panels.composition: Wood staring at the zero. The stick figures have all turned to look at the dog instead. The dog, unbothered, is the only thing in the room anyone wants.

image.prompt: a young man staring at a monitor while every stick figure in the room has turned away to look at a small dog asleep on the floor, no words

art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays in watercolor, improving

notes: The serious page gets zero. The dog gets everyone. The strip knows why; the author doesn't yet.
